description: Over 1,300 square-feet and two loft bedrooms, 33 Carolina Lane – a block once dedicated to agricultural industry, today a multi-cultural gathering spot – offers modern amenities and industrial design, with just the right touch of history: Curated artwork and pops of color, designer furnishings and massive flat-screen TVs, exposed ducts and lofted ceilings – all, in perfect balance with wizened walls and striking wood floors, layered with the patina of the past.

Here, connecting two of the city’s most sought-after streets – W. Walnut and Woodfin/Hiawassee – Carolina Lane is a quiet (for the city) alley, long known to the real Asheville. This is where Oscar winning actress Frances McDormond conspicuously smoked her cigarettes after a day of filming in the area and industry once reigned. And this neighborhood? Well, it’s still a place where restaurants go unadvertised and the best bars have no signs, just a door. A place where high-end art galleries about record shops, upscale shoe stores, and more.

And, while Real Life may be about compromise – sacrifice This to get That – we believe that vacation should be a special time. A time you get both This and That, no compromise required.

host_about:
Growing up Santa Fe, NM I saw a unique blend of artistic community, endless outdoor opportunities, interesting history, beautiful landscapes, and a diverse mix of cultures.

Though far from Santa Fe and a different climate, I arrived in Asheville in the early 90’s to practice Chinese Medicine and felt some of the same elements at play.  Asheville was not well known, but you could feel the energy building and the mixture of art, landscape, environment, history and community all coming together.  It reminded me of my ‘early days’ in Santa Fe.  

One of my closest friends was Andy Brokmeyer, who I told for several years that he needed to come to Asheville, as it was a dynamic and exciting place.  We were also avid kayakers, and Asheville has been a Mecca for kayaking since the early days of the sport so I knew I could lure him out with the promise of all the great rivers in the area. 

He came out ‘for a visit’ and hasn’t left.  That was 16 years ago.  

Asheville has grown into the most happening place in the region, far beyond my expectations, and has sustained an authentic, community oriented and dynamic quality.  Like my dad used to say about few places, it has ‘cultural energy’. 

Though both Andy and I had done some residential real estate investment and development, 80 N Lexington was our first move into the commercial side.  It was an old building, greatly in need of repair, and was a bit removed from the core downtown commercial traffic.  We scraped together what we could and fixed it up, with an eye towards something special in the future. 
 
Now, many years later, North Lexington Ave is hopping, with restaurants, breweries, bars, tea houses, coffee shops, galleries and wonderful, diverse retail shops right out the door.  

And 80 N Lexington has been transformed into a blend of funky, hip, and industrial intertwined with lush, upscale design.  A mix of style and comfort that is unique and authentically Asheville.  

Just like Asheville, there’s nothing quite like it.

name: Terrace Cottage
description: Located in one of Asheville's oldest historic districts, walkable to UNC-Asheville, the Omni Grove Park Inn, restaurants, wine shops, markets, greenways, parks and more! Downtown is walkable on well-lit sidewalks (under 2 miles), a 5-min drive away.
neighborhood_overview: Our beautiful Grove Park Historic District close to downtown is a safe, friendly neighborhood with well-lit sidewalks, wonderful gardens, parks, and a fantastic greenway linking to the center of Asheville.
host_about:
Welcome to Terrace Cottage!

For fifteen years we have enjoyed hosting visitors in our Asheville, North Carolina cottage from across the country and around the world including England and Ireland, Greece, Canada, Mexico and Cuba, Argentina, Japan and The Phillipines. We welcome guests from around the corner, across the US and our international visitors as well! Our college-age daughter grew up listening to many different languages in the driveway.

We enjoy traveling including work-and-play trips to Ireland, England, Sweden and Greece. Twenty years here at our residence built in 1926 and our adjacent Terrace Cottage was built in 2000.

We love working in our perennial beds and veggie gardens.

I'm an online entrepreneur designing and marketing wooden playthings for young people. I also collect and blog about vintage wooden toys.

My wife is a clinician with UNC-Chapel Hill School of Medicine. 

We love living in Asheville and are always happy to return home when away. It is a nationally-celebrated and uniquely beautiful mountain city overflowing with eclectic opportunities for enjoying first-rate dining, entertainment, crafts and artwork. The Blue Ridge Parkway entrance is ten minutes from our home, leading to the North Carolina Arboretum, Mount Pisgah, Craggy Gardens, and Mount Mitchell- the highest elevation east of the Rocky Mountains. 

I fly fish and welcome inquiries regarding our local waters. My favorite streams are under an hour away and have been rated in Trout Unlimited's Top 100. There are excellent fly shops and outfitters nearby if you need them.

Walking, running and cycling are huge in Asheville and there are too many options to mention from neighborhood greenways and hill climbs to maniacal day-longs as well, contact us for info. Our local runner's and cyclist's shops are just blocks away.

Speaking of walkable- ditto our supermarket and specialty/whole foods markets, cafes, coffee shops, local theater, pharmacies, UNC-Asheville, botanical gardens, awesome kid's parks and more.

Thanks for looking at Terrace Cottage and we welcome your inquiries!

name: Cozy Asheville Retreat
description: Welcome to our charming and cozy Airbnb nestled in a tranquil neighborhood, just 1.5 miles away from the vibrant heart of downtown Asheville. With a king-size bed, infrared sauna, a private driveway, and your very own entrance, this inviting space is perfect for up to four adults, offering you the ideal blend of comfort and convenience.
neighborhood_overview:
Our charming basement apartment is situated in a serene and friendly neighborhood, offering a peaceful retreat while being conveniently close to some of Asheville's most delightful dining and entertainment options.

Dining and Culinary Delights:
You'll find an array of culinary delights just a short walk from your doorstep. Whether you're in the mood for artisanal pizza, fresh sushi, health-conscious fare, indulgent ice cream, or the best Italian cuisine in town, our neighborhood has it all:

Asheville Pizza and Brewing Company: A local favorite, known for its delectable pizzas and craft beers.

Zen Sushi: For the sushi enthusiasts, Zen Sushi offers a wide range of fresh and creative sushi rolls.

Green Sage: If you prefer health-conscious options, Green Sage serves up delicious and nourishing meals.

The Hop Ice Cream: Satisfy your sweet tooth with handcrafted ice cream flavors at The Hop.

Avenue M: Experience a delight
host_about:
I followed the whitewater to this beautiful mecca in the mountains.  I love all the amazing opportunities to be in the gorgeous natural beauty of this area.  So many rivers, waterfalls, trails, and views to enjoy.  Asheville also happens to be one of the coolest towns I've ever come across to hang out in.  Southern charm, for sure.  Lots of great live music, delicious restaurants, local festivals, amazing art scene, and a happening dance community.  Oh yeah, a healing arts mecca.  Plenty of yoga and therapeutic options around these parts.
I'll tell you where to find the best huevo rancheros you've ever had in your life!
I've lived in Asheville for 10 years now, and know the area pretty well from all of my exploration.  I have worked at the 5 star resort, The Grove Park Inn, and happen to live just one mile from this world famous Resort and Spa.  Being a massage therapist there, I can tell you which treatments will be perfect for you.  I have spent plenty of time at the Biltmore Estates and can suggest good walks to take there.

description: This studio apartment is only a seven-minute drive to downtown Asheville. Situated at the end of a cul-de-sac, the acre and a half are filled with both flower and vegetable gardens, a large fire pit with plenty of seating (bring your bundle of firewood or ask if I can get for you at a small charge).
neighborhood_overview:
Since I grew up on Cherry Lane, in the house next door, I have many fond and magical memories. Today, it still holds that magic. It's a family centered neighborhood and folks appreciate slow driving on Cherry Lane's small street as there are kids who actually play outside!
My grandparents bought the three acres in 1945 because a double rainbow hung over the eastern view. 10 Cherry Lane was where they lived until my family moved in with them. Four kids and two parents living in the upstairs at 10 had my grandparents moving quickly to build their dream house. 12 was designed by a protege of Frank Lloyd Wright and is a one-of-a-kind style with plenty of light and outside areas for calm meditative moments or kickball. A garden provides fresh heirloom tomatoes, herbs, beans, corn and squash you are welcome to enjoy and use if cooking.

If you want to walk to places, there's a few great restaurants less than a mile away. Moe's Barbaque is down the hill, Cecelia's Argentinian
host_about:
My grandparents built this house in 1959. My grandfather was a Major General, head of the 13th AD, and a graduate of West Point in 1915, along with Eisenhower and Omar Bradley. After getting shot in WW2, his military career ended and he and my grandmother moved to Asheville so he could run the VA Hospital in Oteen. 

The house next door and three acres is what they bought in 1945 after witnessing a double rainbow over the mountains. After my mother and father moved us four kids to the upstairs of that house, my grandparents got an architect who studied with Frank Lloyd Wright to design the mid-century modern house next door, and my childhood was spent going between the houses. 

Four years ago I came up to renovate the place in order to sell it, but after watching a full moon rise over the mountains, I fell in love with it all over again and bought it. It's a comfort knowing this property has never left our family. I can feel all my relations here and enjoy the memories I had, mostly with my loving, brilliant, funny grandmother in this house. It has been a gathering spot for many famous people, including Ike and Mamie, who were close friends of my grandparents, and Carl Sandburg. 

I am an artistic welder and a singer and have travelled all over the world entertaining the troops for the Dept of Defense. Along the path of my travels, I always appreciated the kindness of locals who guided me when lost or recommended flavorful local places set apart from the tourist track. I'm here to offer you the same guidance.

There are sculptures and furniture inside and around my property that I made. 

 I love meeting new people, and I also love my privacy. I respect guests privacy as well and am available with any questions, concerns, interests you may have, but otherwise will not intrude. I live upstairs, and I am sensitive to being quiet. I encourage my guests to feel right at home. 

The expansive yard has plenty of areas to sit and enjoy a cup of coffee or a cocktail. The garden beds have herbs you are welcome to use.

Feel free to text with any questions prior to your stay as well as during your stay. My goal is for everyone who books the studio to enjoy the view, the birds, the wildlife, and the close proximity to everything fun while feeling far away, so much so, that they want to come back!!!

name: Urbane Retreat Cabin In town Asheville 90 DAYS
description:
CHANGE YOUR VIEW FOR WORK or RETIREMENT!

We welcome you with a tradition of Southern hospitality, modern conveniences and an unmatched setting amidst the beauty of Asheville. This urbane retreat where city folks could tap into their inner adventurer.

Lovers of log cabins experience our ongoing commitment to providing an unforgettable experience for our guests who have recognized us with their ★★★★★ Five-Star reviews.

Let our cabin be your home base to explore Asheville today.
neighborhood_overview:
Homeland Park is a neighborhood built as a resort community of about 70 close by log cabins during the 1930s. It offers handcrafted log cabins and cottages each with unique and special characteristics still present, reminding visitors that this uncommon place is indeed one of Asheville’s treasures. These cabins hold fast to their heritage of a time gone by.
This area will charm as you meander through its tree lined streets of oaks and dogwoods, listening to the song birds. Today it is a terrific rental destination or temporary home while relocating. Everything is easy access.
host_about:
Lori and Lizzie who own three 5 Star properties. We are a couple who moved to Asheville, North Carolina from Guatemala, Central America  years ago after living overseas for 5 years. We traveled to Asheville after selling everything and brought our 2 dogs, plus a couple of suitcases. 

Our desire for adventure and travel took us to different countries to experience authentic adventures as well as the vibrant flavors of local food. Travel has shaped our choices.

Like most Ashevillians putting down roots who move here in the melting pot of the south, we have an eclectic mix of people that come from all corners of the country moreover the world to live and thrive in our wonderful southern community. There is so much to offer - experiencing different yummy foods, hiking, biking, artisans of all kinds, and wonderful independent shops as well as breweries, to do what they love and follow their passion. This is palpable in the city, further we feel the connection many have to the area. We think you will too.

We enjoy sharing our passion in a snapshot of Southern hospitality of life in Asheville as well as always striving to enhance our guest's experience. Our guests prefer renting private homes over just a cookie cutter hotel room for a richer experience, thanks to the additional amenities offered in homes. One of the primary goals we have is to offer a truly authentic experience. 

As Superhosts we have welcomed hundreds of guests from many countries. Our philosophy is working hard to focus on attention to detail which is seen in everything we do. This commitment is constantly evolving to offer an unforgettable experience for everyone. Our dreams continue to materialized in the form of having three inviting properties that our guests have recognized us with their 5 Star reviews. It’s an honor to reach this level of recognition as this is vital to our success, in addition to paying a living wage to our team who are an integral part of the guest experience.

We also encourage you to share our listings with your fellow travel enthusiasts, it just might be the first step toward inspiring their own life-changing experience. Should you have any questions about Asheville during your stay at our places, we are always accessible and available. We enjoy working with guests to make it a memorable stay. We are the perfect choice for savvy travelers.

We look forward to helping you with future plans with the true spirit of Asheville. As your host we look forward to welcoming you again and again.

We’re excited to announce that we’re fully restored with water, power, and internet, and ready to welcome guests for stays starting November 2nd and beyond! More than 100 local restaurants are open and Biltmore opens Nov 2nd!

Whether you’re planning a relaxing getaway or need a place to stay while helping with recovery efforts, we’re here and ready to host you!
neighborhood_overview: Quite, peaceful, safe and friendly
host_about:
We moved to Asheville about 13 years ago and love the city and the many travelers who visit! 

We both come from the hospitality industry.

Mike was an Imagineer for Walt Disney World and Disneyland. Tom was an executive at Starbucks Coffee so we know how to provide a great experience for our guests!  

We love dogs and that why we don’t charge a pet fee! 

Over a period of four years we took in what we called “Hospice Dogs” from the local rescue. We provided their medications and gave them super quality of life until they passed. Over those years we cared for a total of seven hospice dogs. While we don’t do it anymore as it’s just too heartbreaking we do have two non-hospice dogs, Buddy a senior Yorker who looks like a well loved teddy bear and Djinn Djinn along haired Chihuahua named after “I Dream of Jeannie” dog.  

All that to say that your dogs are welcome!

description:
Hello!

Our amazing community is rebuilding following Hurricane Helene & we are once again offering our lovely space in Historic Montford, just a short walk to downtown Asheville!

BRAND NEW, spacious & beautifully remodeled this apartment has tons of natural light, its own private entrance & deck.

neighborhood_overview:
The historic neighborhood of Montford is wonderful to explore on foot - gorgeous tree-lined streets, bungalows, parks & trails.

There are a few neighborhood eateries that are gems. My favorite is right around the corner — All Day Darling — open from 7 am to 8 pm every day. Their food is sourced locally and the baked goods are delicious.

If you need a grocery store, Whole Foods, Trader Joe’s and Harris Teeter are within a mile.

Be sure to check out my guidebook where my Asheville favorites are shared.
host_about:

My studio in Asheville is located in Grovewood Village adjacent to the Grove Park Inn. I spend the majority of my time making one-of-a-kind hand-built ceramics.

My home is a treasure to me. I am blessed to have enough space to share it with friends, family and/or Airbnb guests!

name: Bluebirds Nest—sparkling water—cont bkfst—hot tub
description:
Bluebirds Nest is in a great location in the country yet only 10 minutes from downtown Asheville, the Biltmore House, UNCA, Business District, West Asheville, breweries, hiking, rafting, and biking.

Park right outside your own private entrance to this charming place. This spacious and bright space is furnished in French country chic and includes many amenities and a delicious continental breakfast. People from all backgrounds are welcome in Bluebirds Nest.
neighborhood_overview: Born and raised less than a mile from Bluebirds Nest, I know nearby friends and family.  A quiet and safe community, bikers glide by on our road.  Wildlife invade at their own leisurely pace.
host_about:
My husband and I are natives of Asheville.  We love this vibrant city and the beautiful mountains of WNC and love sharing our knowledge and experiences with you.  

I am an artist/educator with a home studio adjacent to Bluebirds Nest.  My paintings are in a gallery in the River Arts District at 310 ART where I have taught workshops. I would be glad to recommend sites and galleries to see while visiting Asheville.

I am a retired teacher from Buncombe County Schools.  National Board Certified, I taught digital imaging, website development, and computer applications.  

My interest in digital imaging led me into photography with the beauty of these WNC mountains and the people and their culture being my favorite subjects.

I come from a railroading family and Southern Railway/Norfolk Southern has been good to us.  The railroad's history is tied to the River Arts District and I felt as if I was "coming home" when I became an exhibiting artist at 310 ART at Riverview Station.

My husband comes from a Coca-Cola family who pioneered Coke in the western most counties including Bryson City.  His aunt married into the Granville Calhoun family and the old homeplace is still standing up Hazel Creek in the Great Smokies National Park.

I enjoy hiking and fishing but my waterskiing days are over!  We especially like to spend long weekends at our houseboat on Fontana Lake with our family.

We have two wonderful daughters, son-in-laws, and three red-headed grandchildren!  

We will be glad to share our knowledge of this area with you and make any recommendations you may be interested in.

Our style of hosting is very simple.  We are here if you need us and want to provide you with the best accommodations possible.  We want you to feel as if you are family.

We invite you to stay with us and hope to see you soon.

Bet

description: My cozy 2 bedroom sleeps 4 lucky folks. Just a couple of minutes walk to trendy West Asheville and a 5 minute drive to downtown Asheville, your vacation will be filled with activities before you know it!
neighborhood_overview:
Where do I begin? West Asheville has everything you could imagine packed into one tiny, walkable space! From nationally known restaurants to fun, relaxed bars, there's really something for everyone here!
If you like a good burger I would have to recommend Universal Joint. This bar/restaurant is in an old converted service station and is one of my all-time favorite places to eat. The Steinbeck burger is loaded with homemade pimento cheese, bacon and pickled (URL HIDDEN) die for! Oh, and did I mention the tater tots? Exquisite. If you're not a burger fan they offer a huge selection of other amazing items. Among the other fantastic bars within walking distance from our house are: UpCountry Brewing, Westville Pub, Brew Pump (this bar is actually in the Citi Stop gas station and hosts a different food truck each night), Oyster House Brewing, WALK and many more!
Among the other fabulous restaurants you'll find: Nine Mile (Jamican), Standard Pizza Co, Sunny Point Cafe (featured on
host_about: I am a hardworking girl looking to travel a bit more! I have taught school for over 11 years. I want to be able to make a few changes to my house and would love the opportunity to travel more. I thought Airbnb would be the perfect opportunity! I have family all over the place right now: a brother in Japan, sister in Colorado, and a cousin in San Fran--all places I love to visit! I love all things silly and quirky especially a good British Comedy or Tom Robbins novel. Much of the reason I love Asheville is for the incredible variety of cheap, delicious food and beer. There's always something to do around town whether it's catching a new independent film, tubing down the French Broad River or tasting a new micro-brew!

Explore the fascinating past at the Riverside Cemetery, where you'll discover poignant gravesites from the Civil War, Spanish American War, WWI, and WWII. Just a short drive away, you'll find the iconic Biltmore Estate and Biltmore Village, both within a 3-mile radius.

Savor the vibrant culinary scene with neighborhood cafes at your doorstep. Indulge in Caribbean-inspired cuisine at Nine Mile or enjoy a delightful al fresco breakfast or lunch at All Day Darling. For art enthusiasts, the renowned River Arts District awaits, with its 22 historic and industrial buildings housing over 200 working artists and studios—all just a few minutes away by car.

Historic Montford offers a captivating blend of heritage, culture, and gastronomy, providing you with an unforgettable experience filled with exploration and inspiration.

name: True Asheville B&B- Wall Street Room- 2nd Floor
description:
Enjoy Asheville at the Chestnut Street Inn, a true B&B just a 10 min walk to downtown Asheville, 10 min drive to the Biltmore Estate and 15 min drive to the Blue Ridge Parkway.
Featured in Food & Wine Magazine, enjoy one of our 8 exquisite bedrooms (all with private baths), delicious homemade breakfast every morning, private en-suite spa treatments, freshly baked cookies in the afternoon, local beer on tap and a rotating house port wine to sip on our incredible porches.
neighborhood_overview: Located in the Chestnut Hill Historical District of Asheville, we are a quick 10 minute walk to downtown and less than a mile from everything it has to offer.
host_about:
Emilie first fell in love with Asheville over 20 years ago when she attended Rockbrook Camp in the heart of a wooded mountain in Brevard, NC. Those mountains, so different from the beaches of her childhood, kept her coming back for ten years. There is something majestic about the Blue Ridge Mountains that blanket Western North Carolina, at over 1 billion years old, they are some of the oldest mountains in the entire world.

Arturo came to Asheville for the first time in 2012 and was quickly enamoured with the outdoor culture, so different from his 22 years in New York City, but so reminiscent of his childhood in the gentle hills of Puebla, Mexico. For him, it was a desire to start a family and a business and seek a better quality of life and he quickly found himself thirsty for everything that Asheville has to offer.

Emilie and Arturo met in 2008 while working together as sommeliers in the Lower East Side of Manhattan at The Ten Bells. Their working relationship was incredible, and over the next six years that relationship became a fine tuned machine- customers would always comment about the way they were able to seamlessly run the entire restaurant without even speaking. Learning the way one another worked over those first six years was the beginning of a true friendship that blossomed into love.

With 35 years of fine dining experience between the two, a Bed and Breakfast seemed like the perfect next adventure. Their penchant for hospitality and intuitive service and their true joy in meeting new people and making new friends put them in a unique position to choose their next path.

Emilie’s first Bed and Breakfast plan was written in the back of a college notebook when she was 18, wandering around Maine searching for the perfect wraparound porch. In 2011, she and Arturo decided to give those Bed and Breakfast dreams a trial run, and opened a small B&B in their East Village apartment. While tiny, it gave them a wonderful test-run on breakfast planning, scheduling, cleaning, decorating, recipe testing and conflict management. They loved it all!

The tri-lingual couple feel that they will bring a new, re-invented experience to the somewhat clichéd country B&B Inn. Asheville is no longer a sleepy town with boarded up buildings, it is a hub of restaurants, nightlife, music, beer and outdoor adventure. It’s not only the perfect place to call home, it is the perfect place to welcome someone into yours.

I went to Western Carolina University in the 90s and visited Asheville on occasion, but it was much different then. In the past 14 years West Asheville has seen a big revival with lots of room to grow. With Sunny point and Biscuit Head restaurant's 3 brewery's right on Haywood rd and near buy and  many other places to eat/visit within a couple of miles.
Therw,are,several green ways and   I love being outside hiking biking or camping,  when I can get away. So I spend most of my time in the shediohouse doing art music or mad scientist stuff.

 So, after enough culture shock back in Atlanta I decided to explore Asheville in the late 90’s. After being here for a week or so wuth my Boxer Buddy I knew I'd found our new home.  I'd also developed a love of old houses growing up in Atlanta so bought this 1927 bungalow from a friend in 2000. 
 In 2006 I decided to create a new space with a view. Only by cleaning my gutters did I notice what a great view to the west there was from a slightly higher perspective. So, I designed and built the “Treetop Loft” and lived up there for many years and rented the downstairs long term. I now love sharing this space and hearing  feedback I get about the design, the light and feel of the space.
 I'm also artist and one of the reasons I moved back downstairs is to have more wall space for the larger paintings I'd missed. 
 I’m an avid motorcyclist, lover of the outdoors and great beer so Asheville has been the perfect home for a long time now! 

  I do hope you enjoy Asheville as much as I do !

name: 80 LEX 201 Exquisite Downtown Apt
description:
This is it.

In a city all about it's micro-neighborhoods, N. Lexington Avenue is The Neighborhood. This is the historic and cultural center of downtown Asheville, once home to farmers and growers and today the heart of all things trendy, artsy and quintessential.

And on hip Lexington Ave., Apartment 201 at 80 LEX – a building once the town's feed and seed warehouse, now its hottest address – is THE place: a 1-bedroom, 1-bath apartment + one free parking space, that breathes Asheville chic.
neighborhood_overview:
Location, Location, Location
If you’ve ever wandered through downtown Asheville, then you’ve felt the wanderlust (and “wonder-lust)” of N. Lexington Avenue.

This is the most hip and quintessential street in Asheville – a place where restaurants go unadvertised and the best bars have no signs, just a door. This is a place where high-end art galleries abut record shops, upscale shoe stores, and more.

And, while Real Life may be about compromise – sacrifice This to get That – we believe that vacation should be a special time. A time you get both This and That, no compromise required.

80 LEX is your no-compromise-required destination: both urban and urbane, situated right in the beating heart of our vibrant city. Enveloped by the energy and excitement of downtown life, Unit 201 embodies and embraces the Asheville scene – a scene that draws designers and artists, creatives and music lovers, foodies and artisanal beverage aficionados alike.
host_about:
Growing up Santa Fe, NM I saw a unique blend of artistic community, endless outdoor opportunities, interesting history, beautiful landscapes, and a diverse mix of cultures.

Though far from Santa Fe and a different climate, I arrived in Asheville in the early 90’s to practice Chinese Medicine and felt some of the same elements at play.  Asheville was not well known, but you could feel the energy building and the mixture of art, landscape, environment, history and community all coming together.  It reminded me of my ‘early days’ in Santa Fe.  

One of my closest friends was Andy Brokmeyer, who I told for several years that he needed to come to Asheville, as it was a dynamic and exciting place.  We were also avid kayakers, and Asheville has been a Mecca for kayaking since the early days of the sport so I knew I could lure him out with the promise of all the great rivers in the area. 

He came out ‘for a visit’ and hasn’t left.  That was 16 years ago.  

Asheville has grown into the most happening place in the region, far beyond my expectations, and has sustained an authentic, community oriented and dynamic quality.  Like my dad used to say about few places, it has ‘cultural energy’. 

Though both Andy and I had done some residential real estate investment and development, 80 N Lexington was our first move into the commercial side.  It was an old building, greatly in need of repair, and was a bit removed from the core downtown commercial traffic.  We scraped together what we could and fixed it up, with an eye towards something special in the future. 
 
Now, many years later, North Lexington Ave is hopping, with restaurants, breweries, bars, tea houses, coffee shops, galleries and wonderful, diverse retail shops right out the door.  

And 80 N Lexington has been transformed into a blend of funky, hip, and industrial intertwined with lush, upscale design.  A mix of style and comfort that is unique and authentically Asheville.  

Just like Asheville, there’s nothing quite like it.

Anyone who uses Airbnb knows you have to invest a lot of time and energy to find the good rentals in Asheville, NC.   The city made it illegal after we got our permits and there are way too many folks trying to book far too few homes.

I have stayed in those before and you are not exactly welcomed by the other homeowners.   The neighbors tend to dislike the constant coming and going of tourists in a family neighborhood.

I once lived next to an illegal Airbnb property and came up with a solution.

We are literally an entire resort of vacation rentals all side by side.   Your neighbor is also here for a special occasion and will probably offer you a beverage.

You can bring anywhere from 1 to 100 people and have the whole place to yourself.

It is without equal.   The best you can do is copy us, but nobody can get the permits.

Bachelorette’s and Wedding Parties got us started but we shy away from them now.   

We will host a lot of different occasions and you need not worry if you want to have a bachelor party or bachelorette.   

I make it no secret that we want to focus on corporate executives who visit for team building and holistic health retreats, but we don't judge your motive.

We welcome everyone the same way.

You can depend on us because we deliver what you are expecting and then we go as far beyond as is humanly possible.

My team has some of the best and brightest.   My right hand is Lesley, my left hand is Aracely, her children Kasey and Brian are her right and left hands.  If something needs repair, Leo & Kaden are available.

I have known each person on my staff from years and years of time together.   I am not easy to work for.   Trust me.   

At times, I have no idea why these people are such hard workers and trusted friends. 
With Covid-19 we all work for a fraction of our former compensation.

Somehow; you and I both got lucky.    We survived this and I see the light at the end of the tunnel.

Ok, I will wrap this up:

If you reach out you will never get an answering service or a stranger.   

We are not property managers.    We are the folks who built this place.

We built it for you.

You don't arrive here by accident.

So far, 217 Airbnb customers have reviewed us.   Keep in mind, that represents thousands of people as our average group is 12 people.

Nobody has ever given us below 5 stars.   Not even once.   Not even close.

Plus, you are welcome to check a lot of other websites and our own internal software.  

Thousands of people have come here and they seem to be happy with us and we often see them again and again.

We cost more for a reason:   

You get more.

You come for a special occasion.   

You leave with a priceless memory.

Then we plan for the next one.

I think that is why we are almost booked out into '22.

All the best,
jay

neighborhood_overview:
Having relocated to Asheville in 2008 we have lived in North, West and for the past several years, East Asheville. We have found by far the traffic flow into and out of Asheville and surrounding area attractions is the easiest from the East. Especially from our Cottage, since the Blue Ridge Parkway is just 1.5 miles away. The Parkway is not only good for hiking and scenic views but also a good shortcut to get to the other side of town!

The Azalea Riceville neighborhood is one of the safest in the Asheville area. It is a mix of new and old houses. A few of our Cottage neighbors have lived here for generations. host_about:
I am a bookkeeper by profession, a nature lover at heart, and a proud mother of a 12 yo girl and 5 yo boy.  My husband, Mark, and I love adventuring in nature and trying new things.  Camping is the most frequent way we adventure.  A boat in campsite on lake Jocassee, in South Carolina, is one of our favorite yearly routines. 

When we are not camping, we do utilize Airbnb as guests in other places.  Airbnb has been such a fun part of our travels!  We loved it when we toured Europe last spring.  It is a delight to be welcomed into each unique place we have stayed and to have that instant connection with a local.  

I grew up in Vermont and have spent time living in, what I feel, are some of the most wonderful places in the United States!  Captiva Island, Fl (on a little house boat), Berkley, CA (across the bay from San Francisco), Tassajara Zen center in Carmel Vally, CA,  Santa Fe, NM and Durango, CO.   

When Mark and I began feeling like we wanted to relocate from Colorado, I thought of the Blue Ridge parkway, which has been a very special place for me since hiking the Appalachian trail in 1999.   We flew out to visit, discovered Asheville (a place I did not visit when thru hiking years ago) and fell in love immediately.  

Having relocated to Asheville in 2008.  Mark and I have lived in North, West and for the past several years, East Asheville.  Asheville is a delightful place that offers so much!  We are very happy to be raising our children here and to have this wonderful place to call home.

name: 80 LEX 202 Iconic Location
description:
80 LEX Apartment 202 : Iconic Downtown Location 1 BD King / 1 BA private apartment at 80 N. Lexington Ave, includes one off street designated parking space, less than a block away.

They say that wherever you go, there you are.

We say, when you go to Asheville, this is where you want to be. Right here, in the heart of Asheville. Right here, on N. Lexington Ave., in a building once home to farmers and growers and today the heart of all things trendy, artsy and quintessential.
neighborhood_overview:
Location, Location, Location
If you’ve ever wandered through downtown Asheville, then you’ve felt the wanderlust (and “wonder-lust)” of N. Lexington Avenue.

This is the most hip and quintessential street in Asheville – a place where restaurants go unadvertised and the best bars have no signs, just a door. This is a place where high-end art galleries abut record shops, upscale shoe stores, and more.

And, while Real Life may be about compromise – sacrifice This to get That – we believe that vacation should be a special time. A time you get both This and That, no compromise required.

80 LEX is your no-compromise-required destination: both urban and urbane, situated right in the beating heart of our vibrant city. Enveloped by the energy and excitement of downtown life, Apartment 202 embodies and embraces the Asheville scene – a scene that draws designers and artists, creatives and music lovers, foodies and artisanal beverage aficionados alike.
host_about:
Growing up Santa Fe, NM I saw a unique blend of artistic community, endless outdoor opportunities, interesting history, beautiful landscapes, and a diverse mix of cultures.

Though far from Santa Fe and a different climate, I arrived in Asheville in the early 90’s to practice Chinese Medicine and felt some of the same elements at play.  Asheville was not well known, but you could feel the energy building and the mixture of art, landscape, environment, history and community all coming together.  It reminded me of my ‘early days’ in Santa Fe.  

One of my closest friends was Andy Brokmeyer, who I told for several years that he needed to come to Asheville, as it was a dynamic and exciting place.  We were also avid kayakers, and Asheville has been a Mecca for kayaking since the early days of the sport so I knew I could lure him out with the promise of all the great rivers in the area. 

He came out ‘for a visit’ and hasn’t left.  That was 16 years ago.  

Asheville has grown into the most happening place in the region, far beyond my expectations, and has sustained an authentic, community oriented and dynamic quality.  Like my dad used to say about few places, it has ‘cultural energy’. 

Though both Andy and I had done some residential real estate investment and development, 80 N Lexington was our first move into the commercial side.  It was an old building, greatly in need of repair, and was a bit removed from the core downtown commercial traffic.  We scraped together what we could and fixed it up, with an eye towards something special in the future. 
 
Now, many years later, North Lexington Ave is hopping, with restaurants, breweries, bars, tea houses, coffee shops, galleries and wonderful, diverse retail shops right out the door.  

And 80 N Lexington has been transformed into a blend of funky, hip, and industrial intertwined with lush, upscale design.  A mix of style and comfort that is unique and authentically Asheville.  

Just like Asheville, there’s nothing quite like it.

neighborhood_overview: The apartment  is on North Lexington Avenue in the heart of downtown Asheville. This is the most hip and quintessential street in the city—a place where restaurants go unadvertised and the best bars have no signs, just a door.
host_about:
Growing up Santa Fe, NM I saw a unique blend of artistic community, endless outdoor opportunities, interesting history, beautiful landscapes, and a diverse mix of cultures.

Though far from Santa Fe and a different climate, I arrived in Asheville in the early 90’s to practice Chinese Medicine and felt some of the same elements at play.  Asheville was not well known, but you could feel the energy building and the mixture of art, landscape, environment, history and community all coming together.  It reminded me of my ‘early days’ in Santa Fe.  

One of my closest friends was Andy Brokmeyer, who I told for several years that he needed to come to Asheville, as it was a dynamic and exciting place.  We were also avid kayakers, and Asheville has been a Mecca for kayaking since the early days of the sport so I knew I could lure him out with the promise of all the great rivers in the area. 

He came out ‘for a visit’ and hasn’t left.  That was 16 years ago.  

Asheville has grown into the most happening place in the region, far beyond my expectations, and has sustained an authentic, community oriented and dynamic quality.  Like my dad used to say about few places, it has ‘cultural energy’. 

Though both Andy and I had done some residential real estate investment and development, 80 N Lexington was our first move into the commercial side.  It was an old building, greatly in need of repair, and was a bit removed from the core downtown commercial traffic.  We scraped together what we could and fixed it up, with an eye towards something special in the future. 
 
Now, many years later, North Lexington Ave is hopping, with restaurants, breweries, bars, tea houses, coffee shops, galleries and wonderful, diverse retail shops right out the door.  

And 80 N Lexington has been transformed into a blend of funky, hip, and industrial intertwined with lush, upscale design.  A mix of style and comfort that is unique and authentically Asheville.  

Just like Asheville, there’s nothing quite like it.

host_about:
My husband, Max and I moved to Asheville, NC, in 2001 and love living here! I was raised in San Miguel de Allende, Mexico, where my father taught photography and journalism at the Instituto Allende. I still have the home there in which I grew up!
I moved to Sausalito, California where I became a Strategy Implementation Consultant. As a bilingual and bicultural person, I was able to work  in 11 countries in Western Europe, South America, and North America. It was a great life, and I met wonderful people from all over the world.    I am also a song-writer and an author, and love music of all kinds from all parts of the world.
     Max was born in L.A., "grew up" in Berkeley, taught high school for many years and then went into the building trades for another lifetime. 
     In 2001, my husband and I moved to Asheville, NC, and we love it! Being in the mountains, in a glorious little town is perfect for us in our retirement phase of life, or our "repurposed" phase, as my husband likes to say.   
     We have two small dogs (a chihuahua mix and a mountain feist, both under 16 pounds). 
     We live on two acres, surrounded by wonderful, local neighbors that we are blessed to have around us.  
     We are foodies, love to cook and love to eat out, and can recommend lots of restaurants, though it's hard to keep up as a new and great one seems toped up every week here!
     We're easy going, like hosting friends, family and our AirBnB guests. Kelle was in the hotel and restaurant business decades ago, and this is a gentle step back into something she found much fun to pursue. 

Life is good, and we would  love to share it with you.

host_about:
Our houses are much nicer than they appear on this site.   Airbnb does not allow us to use our own photographs on two of our listings so you may need to go on our internal website.   It is easy to find us with a simple search for "Upstream way"   That is the name of our street.

We also have lots of cool video and virtual tours.   Lesley, my right hand, has compiled volumes of information on Asheville and travel tips for your visit.

Anyone who uses Airbnb knows you have to invest a lot of time and energy to find the good rentals in Asheville, NC.   The city made it illegal after we got our permits and there are way too many folks trying to book far too few homes.    

We built our new website so you will not get tricked with photoshop.    Our 5 houses on Upstream Way are the real thing.   

My development company built the whole street so we are not like a normal house you find in a random location next door to owner occupied homes in a residential neighborhood.   

I have stayed in those before and you are not exactly welcomed by the other homeowners.   The neighbors tend to dislike the constant coming and going of tourists in a family neighborhood.

I once lived next to an illegal Airbnb property and came up with a solution.

We are literally an entire resort of vacation rentals all side by side.   Your neighbor is also here for a special occasion and will probably offer you a beverage.

You can bring anywhere from 1 to 100 people and have the whole place to yourself.

It is without equal.   The best you can do is copy us, but nobody can get the permits.

Bachelorette’s and Wedding Parties got us started but we shy away from them now.   

We will host a lot of different occasions and you need not worry if you want to have a bachelor party or bachelorette.   

I make it no secret that we want to focus on corporate executives who visit for team building and holistic health retreats, but we don't judge your motive.

We welcome everyone the same way.

You can depend on us because we deliver what you are expecting and then we go as far beyond as is humanly possible.

My team has some of the best and brightest.   My right hand is Lesley, my left hand is Aracely, her children Kasey and Brian are her right and left hands.  If something needs repair, Leo & Kaden are available.

I have known each person on my staff from years and years of time together.   I am not easy to work for.   Trust me.   

At times, I have no idea why these people are such hard workers and trusted friends. 
With Covid-19 we all work for a fraction of our former compensation.

Somehow; you and I both got lucky.    We survived this and I see the light at the end of the tunnel.

Ok, I will wrap this up:

If you reach out you will never get an answering service or a stranger.   

We are not property managers.    We are the folks who built this place.

We built it for you.

You don't arrive here by accident.

So far, 217 Airbnb customers have reviewed us.   Keep in mind, that represents thousands of people as our average group is 12 people.

Nobody has ever given us below 5 stars.   Not even once.   Not even close.

Plus, you are welcome to check a lot of other websites and our own internal software.  

Thousands of people have come here and they seem to be happy with us and we often see them again and again.

We cost more for a reason:   

You get more.

You come for a special occasion.   

You leave with a priceless memory.

Then we plan for the next one.

I think that is why we are almost booked out into '22.

All the best,
jay

Opposite side of the street is Corner Kitchen with fresh farm to table meals. At the bottom of our hill is Fig
host_about:
“Travel changes you. As you move through this life and this world you change things slightly, you leave marks behind, however small. And in return, life—and travel—leaves marks on you.”  – Anthony Bourdain.

We LIVE to travel! Heather spent many years working in the airline industry which allowed us to see 40+ countries. The Anthony Bourdain show “No Reservations”  sums up our travel style. We tend to book the first night to recover from jet lag and then keep the rest of the trip open. We like to see where our travels want to take us. Seeking out the “undiscovered” places and truly connecting with locals is what we are all about. Some of our favorites: Luang Prabang / Bagan / Zanzibar / Bali / Colombia / Ronda (got engaged) / Samana, Dominican Republic (got married) / Chicago / Isla Holbox (shhhh, keep it a secret). Through many of these travels Airbnb has been a big piece of the puzzle.  

The two of us met in Aspen, CO. Heather is originally from Chicago and Mark from Virginia Beach. Although Heather loved city life her wanderlust brought her to Aspen for thirteen years.  Mark had been living in Washington D.C. doing the daily grind as an architect and had heard about a firm in Aspen that was hiring. He jumped on the chance and never looked back!  Aspen was a fantastic place to live and truly enjoy life. It taught us that you can live more simply and have a healthier quality of life. 

After a long stint out west and with a child on the way we decided it was time to be closer to family. We had a list of 30 towns all over the midwest and eastern U.S. which we either visited or did research on. After visiting Asheville we knew it was our next stop in life. Mark has opened his own office and Heather teaches at a creative arts center while studying interior design. Besides continuing to travel, we hike with our son and two dogs as often as possible and love checking out the awesome breweries and restaurants Asheville has to offer. We've also just begun hosting on Airbnb and really enjoy meeting fellow travelers and hosting them in our guest suite. 

We hope to inspire others to get out of their comfort zone and check out other places and people on this amazing planet! 

"Not until we are lost do we begin to understand ourselves." 
- Henry David Thoreau

Our houses are much nicer than they appear on this site.   Airbnb does not allow us to use our own photographs on two of our listings so you may need to go on our internal website.   It is easy to find us with a simple search for "Upstream way"   That is the name of our street.

We also have lots of cool video and virtual tours.   Lesley, my right hand, has compiled volumes of information on Asheville and travel tips for your visit.

Anyone who uses Airbnb knows you have to invest a lot of time and energy to find the good rentals in Asheville, NC.   The city made it illegal after we got our permits and there are way too many folks trying to book far too few homes.    

We built our new website so you will not get tricked with photoshop.    Our 5 houses on Upstream Way are the real thing.   

My development company built the whole street so we are not like a normal house you find in a random location next door to owner occupied homes in a residential neighborhood.   

I have stayed in those before and you are not exactly welcomed by the other homeowners.   The neighbors tend to dislike the constant coming and going of tourists in a family neighborhood.

I once lived next to an illegal Airbnb property and came up with a solution.

We are literally an entire resort of vacation rentals all side by side.   Your neighbor is also here for a special occasion and will probably offer you a beverage.

You can bring anywhere from 1 to 100 people and have the whole place to yourself.

It is without equal.   The best you can do is copy us, but nobody can get the permits.

Bachelorette’s and Wedding Parties got us started but we shy away from them now.   

We will host a lot of different occasions and you need not worry if you want to have a bachelor party or bachelorette.   

I make it no secret that we want to focus on corporate executives who visit for team building and holistic health retreats, but we don't judge your motive.

We welcome everyone the same way.

You can depend on us because we deliver what you are expecting and then we go as far beyond as is humanly possible.

My team has some of the best and brightest.   My right hand is Lesley, my left hand is Aracely, her children Kasey and Brian are her right and left hands.  If something needs repair, Leo & Kaden are available.

I have known each person on my staff from years and years of time together.   I am not easy to work for.   Trust me.   

At times, I have no idea why these people are such hard workers and trusted friends. 
With Covid-19 we all work for a fraction of our former compensation.

Somehow; you and I both got lucky.    We survived this and I see the light at the end of the tunnel.

Ok, I will wrap this up:

If you reach out you will never get an answering service or a stranger.   

We are not property managers.    We are the folks who built this place.

We built it for you.

You don't arrive here by accident.

So far, 217 Airbnb customers have reviewed us.   Keep in mind, that represents thousands of people as our average group is 12 people.

Nobody has ever given us below 5 stars.   Not even once.   Not even close.

Plus, you are welcome to check a lot of other websites and our own internal software.  

Thousands of people have come here and they seem to be happy with us and we often see them again and again.

We cost more for a reason:   

You get more.

You come for a special occasion.   

You leave with a priceless memory.

Then we plan for the next one.

I think that is why we are almost booked out into '22.

All the best,
jay

Life is for loving, sharing and making the world better wherever we can.

host_about:
Born in NC, attended UNC-Chapel Hill and got a degree in Journalism. My mom's side of the family has lived in Western North Carolina for the past century and a half. I have relatives buried in the Riverside Cemetery, which we can see from our backyard.
However, I lived most of my adult life on the West Coast. After college, I drove west in a school bus and eventually landed outside Eugene, OR, next to a creek, grew lots of my food, and had a sewing business, selling at the Saturday Market, Circle of Hands and craft fairs up and down the West Coast.
I have been to all 50 states, Canada, several Central American countries, Caribbean islands and Europe. I LOVE meeting people from all around the world and have studied conflict resolution in large groups of people using World Work. I am a therapist full time, offering massage therapy as well as Bodywisdom Therapy, helping people unravel the messages of their bodies, at a location on Merrimon Avenue. I speak a bit of French and Spanish, but am alas, no longer fluent.
My son and I moved back to WNC several years ago to be near my Mom, who lives in Yancey County. I know some sweet areas to visit around the area and are including them in a notebook in the rooms. 
I love being able to offer people a centrally located place to enjoy what WNC has to offer, as well as a prime walking neighborhood to have access to downtown Asheville hotspots. 
I turned both bedrooms and bathrooms downstairs into places that I would like to visit myself, using art from my own collection, and textures and colors that I love.
We have friends and family over on a regular basis so there is a bit of hustle and bustle at times. If you have children, or like to come and go and appreciate the outdoors, you will fit right in! If you want privacy, the private entrance and keypad will fit your needs. If you want total peace and quiet, I am afraid we won't be your cup of tea.
Living lightly on the earth is a core value for me so we recycle as much as possible, and keep our throwaway consumables to a minimum. 
Life is for loving, sharing and making the world better wherever we can.

Though quite close to downtown, 100 years ago West Asheville was its own town independent of Asheville. As a result, this unique area of town has its own “Mini-Downtown” that is centered around Haywood Rd. For the last few decades this commercial corridor has enjoyed a period of reinvestment by the community and area businesses. Several cool and unique restaurants, coffee shops, bars, bakeries, breweries and shops have chosen West Asheville as their home. Century old houses are being renovated back to life and new homes are being built on every available lot. As the historic town of “West Asheville” was never very big, the entire area is very walkable and there are lots of cool old buildings, churches, trees and houses.
The River Arts District and New Belgium Brewing are a 5 minute drive, Biltmore Estate is a 15 minute drive

name: The Woodfin - Chateau de Bro & Chalet de Bae
description:
THE SPACE IS ALL YOURS!

The Woodfin is a chateau de bro, chalet de bae, camp for champs, and home for the roaming adventurer. Nestled in a quiet neighborhood just a 5 to 7-minute drive from downtown, this private dream pad is the perfect hub for couples, friends, and family to explore everything Asheville. Recharge in the high-end Tempurpedic TEMPUR-Cloud® bed for an unbeatable nights sleep! Fully equipped kitchen. Professionally cleaned!!
neighborhood_overview: The small town of Woodfin, NC rests along the banks of the French Broad River and its convenient location next to I-26 makes for a quick 5-minute drive to downtown Asheville. Filled with grit and charm, this historic suburban neighborhood is currently undergoing a fast-paced revival with the expansion of the River Arts District (RAD) and French Broad River Greenway Project. Breweries, restaurants, and coffee shops are overflowing from the nearby RAD.  Our neighbors are lively and friendly, and you’re likely to get a small-town wave. These are good people. Please respect our neighbors by driving slow.
host_about:
I grew up on the Texas border near South Padre Island. I moved to Asheville in (Phone number hidden by Airbnb) from Austin, TX soon after graduating with a degree in mechanical engineering. The mountains called my name, and my would-be manager also called my name (to offer me a job),  so I set out on the 17hr drive and only looked back once...because I thought I saw a bear.

 I began my career servicing CTs, MRIs, and X-ray systems throughout Western North Carolina. If I'm not working on the house or hanging with the fam, my free time is spent playing outdoors - kayak fishing, mountain biking, and rock climbing. 

If there's an opportunity to go fishing, I usually take the bait. I own a small fleet of fishing kayaks and like to take day trips out on the local waters to pursue bass, trout and gorgeous scenery. If you're in the neighborhood to catch some fish, let me know and Ill try to give you some tips on where to go. 

Asheville is a mountain biker's paradise. There's an expansive network of trail systems all throughout the surrounding forests lands and hitting the trails with the gang is a surefire way to put a smile on my face. IMO its the best way to submerse yourself in these mountains and take in all their beauty. If you're itching for a thrilling downhill adventure or a casual bike ride through the mountains, reach out and I can point you in the right direction. 

My relationship with rock climbing is fickle; I'm either climbing or I'm not. I love it because by nature it puts you by nature. But if the fish are biting, its hard to pull me from a kayak to climb a 300 ft bluff. 

I also love music, food, and beer. If Asheville's beer and culinary scene is what brought you here, I am happy to offer advice. Let me know!

host_about:
Hey - I'm Christine.

I moved to Asheville in the early 90's to escape Northern Virginia and my post-college cubicle job. I wanted to be a songwriter...which, as you can guess, thrilled my parents to no end.

In 2010, as a result of requests from so many creative entrepreneurial types (and being burnt out from 250 days a year on the road), I started a business coaching company here in Asheville. That became an online training resource, and we've hosted clients from all over the world at our retreats and events here. These days, I spend more time on Zoom than anything else. :)

Hosting guests has been an unexpected joy and new passion for me.  I love being able to provide all the amenities and experiences for travelers and vacationers and work-from-homers... mostly based on 15 years of staying in every hotel (ahem, and motel) chain and city across the U.S.  I'm still learning so much.

I love all things nature. Trees, birds, bears, mountains, dirt. I strive to contribute the creative and natural spirit of this precious area, even as it grows at a crazy pace.

name: "Albergue" Home base for exploring Asheville & WNC
description: Our home is in charming Montford just north of downtown Asheville.  Our lower level guest suite has its own private entry to come and go as you please. The open floor plan has a queen bed, lounge space  with fold out double sofa), Wifi & TV, table w/ chairs, and kitchenette with fridge, microwave, coffee and toaster.  You'll spend most your time out exploring, and as locals, we offer tips for the outdoors, food, activities, and other unique local favorites.
neighborhood_overview: We are located 1.3 miles from downtown, and even if you don't consider that as "walkable" as we do, we encourage everyone to try it if the weather permits, as it passes through Montford, on the same streets that the tourist trolleys drive down to see the historic homes.  We love our immediate neighborhood for its walkability, unique homes from different time periods, tree-filled tranquility and friendly neighbors.  Even the black bears are regular visitors (we've seen them more in our neighborhood than we have in years of hiking in the mountains).  They are always docile, just sniffing around for food, and will go on their way peacefully if they are not antagonized.  As for or human food, there are several neighborhood restaurants that are walkable, the closest being Nine Mile (Jamaican themed) which is one of Asheville's most popular.
host_about: I've traveled a good bit for both personal and work reasons, and the travel I've most enjoyed has been culturally immersive travels and living short stints in other countries.  I work as an educational travel planner and history tour guide.  Living in a really cool city amid natural scenery has allowed me to also play host.  I enjoy giving tips on the things I enjoy in my area - mountain trails, music venues, microbreweries, eclectic restaurants, dancing, festivals, urban walking/biking/running, water activities.  The same things I'll enjoy doing/exploring in your area.

neighborhood_overview:
LOCATION, LOCATION, LOCATION!
If you’ve ever wandered through downtown Asheville, then you’ve felt the wanderlust (and “wonder-lust)” of this historic warren.

Here, connecting two of the city’s most sought-after streets – W. Walnut and Woodfin/Hiawassee – Carolina Lane is a quiet (for the city) alley, long known to the real Asheville. This is where Oscar winning actress Frances McDormond conspicuously smoked her cigarettes after a day of filming in the area and industry once reigned. And this neighborhood? Well, it’s still a place where restaurants go unadvertised and the best bars have no signs, just a door. A place where high-end art galleries about record shops, upscale shoe stores, and more.

And, while Real Life may be about compromise – sacrifice This to get That – we believe that vacation should be a special time. A time you get both This and That, no compromise required.

35 Caroline Lane is your no-compromise-required destination: both urban
host_about:
Growing up Santa Fe, NM I saw a unique blend of artistic community, endless outdoor opportunities, interesting history, beautiful landscapes, and a diverse mix of cultures.

Though far from Santa Fe and a different climate, I arrived in Asheville in the early 90’s to practice Chinese Medicine and felt some of the same elements at play.  Asheville was not well known, but you could feel the energy building and the mixture of art, landscape, environment, history and community all coming together.  It reminded me of my ‘early days’ in Santa Fe.  

One of my closest friends was Andy Brokmeyer, who I told for several years that he needed to come to Asheville, as it was a dynamic and exciting place.  We were also avid kayakers, and Asheville has been a Mecca for kayaking since the early days of the sport so I knew I could lure him out with the promise of all the great rivers in the area. 

He came out ‘for a visit’ and hasn’t left.  That was 16 years ago.  

Asheville has grown into the most happening place in the region, far beyond my expectations, and has sustained an authentic, community oriented and dynamic quality.  Like my dad used to say about few places, it has ‘cultural energy’. 

Though both Andy and I had done some residential real estate investment and development, 80 N Lexington was our first move into the commercial side.  It was an old building, greatly in need of repair, and was a bit removed from the core downtown commercial traffic.  We scraped together what we could and fixed it up, with an eye towards something special in the future. 
 
Now, many years later, North Lexington Ave is hopping, with restaurants, breweries, bars, tea houses, coffee shops, galleries and wonderful, diverse retail shops right out the door.  

And 80 N Lexington has been transformed into a blend of funky, hip, and industrial intertwined with lush, upscale design.  A mix of style and comfort that is unique and authentically Asheville.  

Just like Asheville, there’s nothing quite like it.

neighborhood_overview:
The Montford Area Historic District is one of the prettiest neighborhoods in the country--though we're admittedly a little biased. Most of the neighborhood's residences were constructed between 1890 and 1920 in the Victorian or Queen Anne Victorian styles, though you'll also find architecture in the Arts and Crafts, Neoclassical, and Colonial Revival styles. Residents pride themselves on their gardening and landscaping expertise, benefited in no small part by the region's capacity for growing an incredible diversity of flora, from the signature magnolia trees, to flowering shrubs like the rhododendron & azalea, to bamboo, succulents, and so much more.

The gorgeous local cemetery is worth a visit, marking the final resting place of authors Thomas Wolfe and O. Henry. North Montford was once home to the Highland Hospital, in which Zelda Fitzgerald tragically died in a fire in 1948.

neighborhood_overview:
Located in East Asheville in the 28805 zip code, Haw Creek was named for the native Black Haw shrub or small tree (Viburnum prunifolium) that grew more abundantly years ago along the moist soils of the valley, especially along Haw Creek itself.

Haw Creek valley’s southern boundary extends from US Highway 70/Tunnel Road at I-240 eastward along Tunnel Road to Maple Springs Road. Its west boundary is formed by Piney Mountain/Bear Mountain ridge; Town Mountain creates the northern boundary; and the Blue Ridge Parkway stretches along most of its eastern border.

Haw Creek was settled in the early 1800’s as a farming community with the first school established in 1842 on the site of the present day Bethesda Cemetery. neighborhood_overview:
Just across the French Broad River from downtown, West Asheville (28806) is a mecca for originality. For the past few years, people have flocked to this funky neighborhood, either to visit or buy a quaint cottage within walking distance of the many new businesses that have opened in the area.

Haywood Road has been the main street of West Asheville for more than a century. Old buildings are now home to modern businesses, but the street still has a small hometown feel. As you walk down the street, you will see old buildings renovated for new businesses side-by-side with second- and third-generation shops. There are now many restaurants, breweries, pubs with frequent live music, bakeries, a variety of resale consignment shops, vintage clothing boutiques and even a half-dozen record shops lining the road that appeal to visitors interested in sampling the unique, bohemian flavor of Asheville.

host_about:
I grew up on the Texas border near South Padre Island. I moved to Asheville in (Phone number hidden by Airbnb) from Austin, TX soon after graduating with a degree in mechanical engineering. The mountains called my name, and my would-be manager also called my name (to offer me a job),  so I set out on the 17hr drive and only looked back once...because I thought I saw a bear.

 I began my career servicing CTs, MRIs, and X-ray systems throughout Western North Carolina. If I'm not working on the house or hanging with the fam, my free time is spent playing outdoors - kayak fishing, mountain biking, and rock climbing. 

If there's an opportunity to go fishing, I usually take the bait. I own a small fleet of fishing kayaks and like to take day trips out on the local waters to pursue bass, trout and gorgeous scenery. If you're in the neighborhood to catch some fish, let me know and Ill try to give you some tips on where to go. 

Asheville is a mountain biker's paradise. There's an expansive network of trail systems all throughout the surrounding forests lands and hitting the trails with the gang is a surefire way to put a smile on my face. IMO its the best way to submerse yourself in these mountains and take in all their beauty. If you're itching for a thrilling downhill adventure or a casual bike ride through the mountains, reach out and I can point you in the right direction. 

My relationship with rock climbing is fickle; I'm either climbing or I'm not. I love it because by nature it puts you by nature. But if the fish are biting, its hard to pull me from a kayak to climb a 300 ft bluff. 

I also love music, food, and beer. If Asheville's beer and culinary scene is what brought you here, I am happy to offer advice. Let me know!

The community was originally located on the present Biltmore Estate until 1889 when it was moved to it's current location in South Asheville. The community is rich in Asheville history, with many families calling this land home since the 1890's.

Today the Shiloh community is a diverse neighborhood with a focus on creating a better future for its residents. We have a beautiful community garden with flowers and vegetables, community center, park, amphitheater, and it is all cared for, and kept by local residents. The neighborhood hosts multiple block parties throughout the year - Halloween, 4th of July, multiple ice cream socials, greenway clean-up days, etc...

To learn more about our neighborhood and upcoming events, visit malvernhills dot org. The archive section has great info on the history of both our neighborhood and West Asheville.

name: Montford Charm - 3BR Monthly Rental
description: Enjoy Asheville like a local by staying in one of its most desired and historic neighborhoods flanking downtown.  This is our sole home, not a vacation rental, that we make available during our long summer travels.  We have managed our basement suite as a popular airbnb for over 3 years, but for a stay of a month plus, we are offering our entire home, including the suite (it will not be rented separately during your stay).  We love our neighbors and neighborhood, and you will too.
neighborhood_overview: We often feel like we're in a movie set walking our neighborhood, full of charming houses of various styles with expansive front porches, mature trees, and nice landscaping.  Our friendly neighbors are often out walking themselves, their dogs, or their children.  We're not far from downtown (1.5 miles) when we want to experience more of Asheville's tourist hustle and bustle, but also very glad that a few of Asheville's favorite eateries are just a pleasant walk away in our neighborhood without needing to go into downtown.  At home, we like sitting on the front porch as neighbors stroll past, or on the side deck or sun room overlooking the wooded back yard.  We love walking in our neighborhood, as it is safe, friendly, and all of the houses of diverse and original styles.
host_about: I've traveled a good bit for both personal and work reasons, and the travel I've most enjoyed has been culturally immersive travels and living short stints in other countries.  I work as an educational travel planner and history tour guide.  Living in a really cool city amid natural scenery has allowed me to also play host.  I enjoy giving tips on the things I enjoy in my area - mountain trails, music venues, microbreweries, eclectic restaurants, dancing, festivals, urban walking/biking/running, water activities.  The same things I'll enjoy doing/exploring in your area.

name: Robins Nest—AVL/Biltmore—fp—ct bkfst—hot tub
description: Forget your worries in this spacious and serene space.
host_about:
My husband and I are natives of Asheville.  We love this vibrant city and the beautiful mountains of WNC and love sharing our knowledge and experiences with you.  

I am an artist/educator with a home studio adjacent to Bluebirds Nest.  My paintings are in a gallery in the River Arts District at 310 ART where I have taught workshops. I would be glad to recommend sites and galleries to see while visiting Asheville.

I am a retired teacher from Buncombe County Schools.  National Board Certified, I taught digital imaging, website development, and computer applications.  

My interest in digital imaging led me into photography with the beauty of these WNC mountains and the people and their culture being my favorite subjects.

I come from a railroading family and Southern Railway/Norfolk Southern has been good to us.  The railroad's history is tied to the River Arts District and I felt as if I was "coming home" when I became an exhibiting artist at 310 ART at Riverview Station.

My husband comes from a Coca-Cola family who pioneered Coke in the western most counties including Bryson City.  His aunt married into the Granville Calhoun family and the old homeplace is still standing up Hazel Creek in the Great Smokies National Park.

I enjoy hiking and fishing but my waterskiing days are over!  We especially like to spend long weekends at our houseboat on Fontana Lake with our family.

We have two wonderful daughters, son-in-laws, and three red-headed grandchildren!  

We will be glad to share our knowledge of this area with you and make any recommendations you may be interested in.

Our style of hosting is very simple.  We are here if you need us and want to provide you with the best accommodations possible.  We want you to feel as if you are family.

We invite you to stay with us and hope to see you soon.

Bet

neighborhood_overview:
The Montford neighborhood is the largest and one of the oldest historic designated areas in Asheville encompassing ≈30 sq blocks of mature tree-lined streets bordering downtown. The majority of these 1890-1920 homes have undergone some degree of renovation in the last 10 years with an influx of young families. Dog walking /baby strolling is a very popular pastime in this neighborhood which is very safe. The Asheville trolley, accessed at the visitor information center (0.5 mile away) can be seen 2 x day making it's way along the main streets here.

There are MANY attractions very closeby. One of the most beautiful and large cemeteries in the southeast is Riverside, where the writer Thomas Wolfe is interred, is in Montford.

description: UPDATE: After Helene, we’re happy to report no damage and are ready to host! Previously managed by a company for six years, we’re now hosting Hidden Creek Craftsman Retreat ourselves and look forward to welcoming you. This unique 7-bedroom, 6.5-bath escape in Chunns Cove, just minutes from downtown Asheville’s dining, shopping, and breweries, sleeps 16+ and blends mountain serenity with modern comforts—spacious decks, a hot tub, and fire pit—all close to Asheville’s best attractions!
neighborhood_overview:
If you're seeking an Asheville neighborhood that combines rural charm with modern convenience, Chunns Cove is the perfect choice. Nestled between Town Mountain/Downtown Asheville to the west, Haw Creek/Sondley Estates to the east, and the Tunnel Road shopping corridor to the south, Chunns Cove is celebrated for its scenic beauty and spacious homes. The area features a range of residences, from classic 1960s ranch-style houses to custom-built homes. As you ascend through the rolling hills, you'll encounter beautifully landscaped properties offering stunning views of the Blue Ridge Mountains.

Winding through Chunns Cove, it's easy to forget how close you are to the amenities below. The neighborhood is characterized by its mature trees and lush greenery, which enhance the sense of seclusion. The generous lot sizes provide ample space for children to play and for creating beautiful gardens. Residents also enjoy observing diverse wildlife in the neighborhood's wooded areas.
host_about: I'm a nature enthusiast who loves cycling, hiking, bikepacking, and vipassana meditation. Originally from Washington State, I moved to Asheville in 2020, enjoying both city and mountain life. Proud parent of a teen, married to an amazing husband, and a passionate college basketball fan. Whether cycling or hiking, I find peace in adventure and the great outdoors.

Hello there!

I grew up in India, a land of diverse languages, cultures, and terrain, and lived in the United States as a software engineer all my adult life working and traveling. I have been a wanderlust all my life. I enjoy traveling to new places, meeting new people, trying new cuisines, and experiencing different cultures.

My philosophy can be summed up in the ancient Sanskrit phrase “Athithi devo bhava” which has profound significance in Hindusim and India. Atithi is a guest who can visit us at any time. Devo Bhava means God-like. Thus, Atithi Devo Bhava indicates that we must consider our guests equivalent to God and care for them.

Feel free to book or message me first; I am friendly, outgoing, and happy to answer any specific questions in advance.

I am a well-traveled guest who knows what hosts should do to create a comfortable experience. My goal is to fulfill these requirements for every guest.

Hope to host you soon!
